approachQuestion.prompt:
Sample Retention

A laboratory stores integer sample labels in a nondecreasing mutable array labels. Keep at most two occurrences of each label, preserving their order, in the beginning of the same array. Return the retained length k. Only labels[0:k] is inspected; the remaining cells may contain anything. Do not resize the array.

Constraints: 0 <= n = labels.length <= 200000; labels[i] is in [-1000000, 1000000].

Example 1: labels = [1,1,1,2,2,2,2,5] -> k = 5, prefix [1,1,2,2,5].
Example 2: labels = [-4,-4] -> k = 2, prefix [-4,-4].
Example 3: labels = [] -> k = 0, prefix [].
constraints: Choose the most efficient valid approach for the entire stated input domain; accept equivalent optimal variants.

options.text: Scan from left to right with a write index w starting at zero. Keep the current label if w < 2 or it differs from labels[w-2]; write it at w and increment w. Return w.
options.feedback: The already retained prefix determines whether two copies of this value have been kept; writes never reach beyond the current read position.

options.text: Copy all labels, scan that copy to collect at most two of each value in a separate buffer, then copy that buffer into the original prefix and return its length.
options.feedback: This always produces the required prefix, but both buffers can be eliminated by writing into the space already passed by the reader.

options.text: Keep only the first occurrence of each label and return the number of distinct labels.
options.feedback: For [7,7], both occurrences must remain. Returning one discards an allowed occurrence.

options.text: Whenever a run has more than two entries, delete each surplus entry by shifting every later active entry one cell left; maintain a logical length without resizing.
options.feedback: It returns the right prefix, but a long repeated run followed by a long suffix repeatedly moves that suffix. Those repeated shifts are avoidable.

feedback.reason: Keep at most two copies of each sorted value in a stable in-place prefix without overwriting unread input.
details: Read the original positions from left to right. The first two accepted values are always retained. Thereafter, accept a value only when it differs from the value two positions before the next output position. Write each accepted value into that output position.
The retained prefix enforces the quota. Comparing two positions behind the write boundary preserves up to two copies without consulting source cells that earlier writes may already have changed.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method revealed after question 1, choose its tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair, with n equal to the original input length. Use a word-RAM model with constant-time indexed reads, writes, comparisons, and signed 64-bit arithmetic. Include every temporary buffer, copy, and call frame. The fixed method is iterative, makes no input copy, uses no hashing, and performs no amortized data-structure operations. Exclude the supplied input and returned scalar; include all other storage. No recursion, slices, or allocated work arrays are used.
constraints: Choose the tightest pair for this fixed method, regardless of the approach you selected in question 1.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: One read pass and bounded writes use fixed pointer state.
details: The read index passes n entries once, with fixed work per entry. Even all-distinct input requires n reads and writes. The write index never exceeds the read index, so no unread value is destroyed.

Use a word-RAM model with constant-time indexed reads, writes, comparisons, and signed 64-bit arithmetic. Include every temporary buffer, copy, and call frame. The fixed method is iterative, makes no input copy, uses no hashing, and performs no amortized data-structure operations. Exclude the supplied input and returned scalar; include all other storage. No recursion, slices, or allocated work arrays are used.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This adds a size-dependent temporary copy or buffer absent from the fixed method.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The method does not restart a full scan for each element; its bounded number of forward or inward scans is linear.
“O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: No sorting or repeated binary searches occur in the fixed method.
